takeaway: Cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to the pCO2 of the perfusing blood; the circle of Willis lets other arteries supply the brain if one blocks.

question.text: With regard to the cerebral circulation:
question.say: With regard to the cerebral circulation, which statement is true?

answer.text: Cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to changes in the pCO2 of the perfusing blood
answer.say: The answer: cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to changes in the pCO2 of the perfusing blood.

lines.text: The brain sits above a roundabout: the circle of Willis.
lines.say: The brain sits above a busy roundabout. This is the circle of Willis, around the base of the brain.

lines.text: All the main arteries connect to it.
lines.say: All the main arteries to the brain connect to this rich anastomosis.

lines.text: If one road blocks, the others still supply the brain.
lines.say: So if one artery blocks, the brain is still supplied by the others. There are no functional end-arteries.

lines.text: The CO2 character turns the tap: flow follows the pCO2.
lines.say: (laugh) And the carbon dioxide character turns the tap. Cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to changes in pCO2.
Cerebral blood flow is little affected by cardiovascular reflexes.

lines.text: Remember: cerebral blood flow follows the pCO2.
lines.say: Remember: cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to the pCO2 of the blood.
